You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

import subprocess, os, sys

def run(args, cwd=".", env_extra=None):
    env = dict(os.environ)
    if env_extra:
        env.update(env_extra)
    # ensure no color forcing? let's see
    p = subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
    return p

for args in [[], ["--help"], ["-h"], ["--version"]]:
    pass

# try various flags
tests = [
    ["--det", "all", "."],
    ["-d", "all"],
    ["--det=all"],
    ["-dall"],
    ["--grid=true"],
    ["-g"],
    ["-g=true"],
    ["--typ=dir"],
    ["-t", "dir"],
    ["--sort=name"],
    ["-s", "name"],
    ["--imp=1"],
    ["-I1"],
    ["--exclude=*.rs"],
    ["--only=*.md"],
    ["--header=false"],
    ["--unit=decimal"],
]

for a in tests:
    p = run(a)
    print(f"$ pls {' '.join(a)} => exit={p.returncode} stdout={repr(p.stdout[:500])} stderr={repr(p.stderr[:500])}")
    print("---")

    # 80x24

    # read with timeout
    import select
    while True:
        r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], [], 1.0)
        if r:
            try:
                data=os.read(master, 8192)
                if not data:
                    break
                out+=data
            except OSError:

        # check if process done

            # drain
            try:
                import fcntl
                flags=fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_GETFL)

                        out+=d

import subprocess, tempfile, os, stat
EXE="/workspace/executable"
def run(args, cwd="/tmp"):
    p=subprocess.run([EXE]+args, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return p.stdout, p.stderr, p.returncode
import tempfile
td=tempfile.mkdtemp()
os.makedirs(f"{td}/noperm", exist_ok=True)
open(f"{td}/noperm/file","w").write("x")
os.chmod(f"{td}/noperm", 0o000)
print(oct(os.stat(f"{td}/noperm").st_mode))
out,err,rc=run(["noperm"], cwd=td)
print(f"noperm => {repr(out)} err={repr(err)} rc={rc}")
# restore
os.chmod(f"{td}/noperm", 0o755)
# test file with no read perm?
open(f"{td}/noread","w").write("x")
os.chmod(f"{td}/noread", 0o000)
out,err,rc=run(["noread"], cwd=td)
print(f"noread file => {repr(out)}")
print(subprocess.run(["ls","-l",td], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout)
# test det for noread?
out,err,rc=run(["--det","size","noread"], cwd=td)
print(f"det noread => {repr(out)}")
os.chmod(f"{td}/noread", 0o644)
# test error for dir with no perm as one of multiple?
os.chmod(f"{td}/noperm", 0o000)
out,err,rc=run(["noperm","noread"], cwd=td)
print(f"multi => {repr(out)}")
os.chmod(f"{td}/noperm", 0o755)
PY

import subprocess, tempfile, os
EXE="/workspace/executable"
def run(args, cwd):
    p=subprocess.run([EXE]+args, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return p.stdout
import tempfile
# Test Cargo with dirs
for files in [
    ["Cargo.toml","Cargo.lock","src"],
    ["Cargo.toml","src"],
    ["Cargo.toml","target"],
    ["Cargo.toml","Cargo.lock","target"],
    ["package.json","node_modules"],
    ["package.json","package-lock.json","node_modules"],
    [".gitignore",".git"],  # .git hidden anyway
    ["a.txt","a.txt:Zone.Identifier"],  # ADS?
]:
    t=tempfile.mkdtemp()
    for f in files:
        if f in ["src","target","node_modules"]:
            os.makedirs(f"{t}/{f}", exist_ok=True)
            open(f"{t}/{f}/dummy","w").write("x")
        else:
            open(f"{t}/{f}","w").write("x")
    print(f"{files} => true {repr(run(['--collapse','true'], cwd=t))} false {repr(run(['--collapse','false'], cwd=t))}")
PY"}

pub fn terminal_size() -> Option<(Width, Height)> {
    // try ioctl on stdout (fd 1)
    unsafe {
        let mut ws: libc::winsize = std::mem::zeroed();
        // need libc crate
        if libc::ioctl(1, libc::TIOCGWINSZ, &mut ws) == 0 && ws.ws_col != 0 {
            return Some((Width(ws.ws_col), Height(ws.ws_row)));
        }
        if libc::ioctl(2, libc::TIOCGWINSZ, &mut ws) == 0 && ws.ws_col != 0 {
            return Some((Width(ws.ws_col), Height(ws.ws_row)));
        }
    }
    None

def run_pty(args, cwd, env_extra=None):
    import pty, os, subprocess, select, struct, fcntl, termios
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", 24, 80, 0, 0))
    e=dict(os.environ)
    if env_extra: e.update(env_extra)
    p=subprocess.Popen([EXE]+args, cwd=cwd, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, env=e)

        if r:
            try:
                d=_os.read(master,16384)
                if not d: break
                out+=d
            except: break
        if p.poll() is not None:
            try:
                flags=fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_GETFL)
                fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_SETFL, flags|_os.O_NONBLOCK)
                while True:
                    try:
                        d=_os.read(master,16384)
                        if not d: break
                        out+=d
                    except: break
            except: pass
            break
    _os.close(master)
    p.wait()
    return out

fn icon_for(node: &Node) -> &'static str {
    // dirs
    if node.file_type=="dir" {
        if node.name=="src" { return "\u{f40d}"; }
        if node.name==".github" { return "\u{f408}"; }
        return "\u{f07b}";
    }
    if node.file_type=="symlink" { return "\u{f0339}"; }
    if node.file_type=="fifo" { return "\u{f07e5}"; }
    if node.file_type=="socket" { return "\u{f07e8}"; }
    if node.file_type=="block-device" { return "\u{f0a0}"; } // guess? need to check block icon
    if node.file_type=="char-device" { return "\u{f1dd}"; } // from /dev test, char icon  (U+F1DD)
    // files: exact and prefix
    let name = node.name.as_str();
    if name=="Dockerfile" || name.starts_with("Dockerfile") { return "\u{f4b7}"; }
    if name=="Makefile" { return "\u{f070e}"; }
    if name=="LICENSE" || name.starts_with("LICENSE.") || name.starts_with("LICENSE-") { return "\u{f495}"; }
    if name=="README" || name.starts_with("README.") || name.starts_with("README-") { return "\u{f02d}"; }
    if name=="Cargo.toml" { return "\u{f487}"; }
    if name=="Cargo.lock" { return "\u{f456}"; }
    if name==".gitignore" { return "\u{f02a2}"; }
    if name==".env" || name.starts_with(".env.") || name.starts_with(".env-") { return "\u{e22f}"; }
    if name=="src" { return "\u{f40d}"; }
    // extensions
    if let Some(ext) = ext_for_icon(name) {
        match ext {
            "rs" => return "\u{e68b}",
            "json"|"yaml"|"yml"|"toml" => return "\u{e60b}",
            "ini" => return "\u{e615}",
            "md" => return "\u{f48a}",
            "txt" => return "\u{e612}",
            "sh" => return "\u{f489}",
            "png"|"jpg"|"jpeg"|"gif"|"svg"|"ico" => return "\u{f02e9}",
            "mp3"|"wav"|"flac"|"ogg" => return "\u{f04c3}",
            "mp4"|"avi"|"mkv"|"mov" => return "\u{f0567}",
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    ""
}
fn ext_for_icon(name: &str) -> Option<&str> {
    // for "a.tar.gz" => "gz"? For ".hidden" => None? For "Dockerfile.dev" => "dev"? But Dockerfile already handled via prefix, so ext not needed.
    // If name starts with '.' and has no other dot, no ext.
    if let Some(pos)=name.rfind('.') {
        if pos==0 { return None; }
        // check if after dot is empty? e.g., "foo." => ""? Return None?
        if pos+1>=name.len() { return None; }
        return Some(&name[pos+1..]);
    }
    None
}
fn suffix_for(node: &Node) -> &'static str {
    match node.file_type.as_str() {
        "dir" => "/",
        "symlink" => "@",
        "fifo" => "|",
        "socket" => "=",
        _ => "",
    }

def run(exe, args, cwd="/tmp"):

# Create test dir
import tempfile
td=tempfile.mkdtemp()
os.makedirs(f"{td}/mydir", exist_ok=True)
open(f"{td}/myfile.txt","w").write("hello")
open(f"{td}/.hidden","w").write("x")

os.symlink("nonexistent", f"{td}/broken")
os.mkfifo(f"{td}/myfifo")

open(f"{td}/Cargo.toml","w").write("x")
open(f"{td}/Cargo.lock","w").write("x")
open(f"{td}/README.md","w").write("x")

tests=[
    [],
    ["--det","all"],
    ["--det","std"],
    ["--det","size"],
    ["--det","perm","--det","oct"],
    ["--icon","false"],
    ["--suffix","false"],
    ["--sym","false"],
    ["--collapse","false"],
    ["--collapse","true"],
    ["--align","false"],
    ["--typ","dir"],
    ["--typ","file"],
    ["--typ","symlink"],
    ["--imp","0"],
    ["--imp","1"],
    ["--imp","2"],
    ["--exclude","my.*"],
    ["--only","my.*"],
    ["--sort","size"],
    ["--sort","name"],
    ["--sort","size_"],

    ["--unit","none","--det","size"],

    ["--sort","inode_"],
    ["--sort","nlinks_"],
]

    rc2,out2,err2=run(NEW, args, cwd=td)

    # For panic cases, rc is -6 (signal), need to compare stderr (which includes thread id, which differs). So for those, check only that both panic (rc negative) and stderr contains panic message (without thread id)?
    if args in [["--sort","inode_"],["--sort","nlinks_"]]:
        # both should panic (rc negative) - thread id differs, so compare without numbers?
        import re
        # normalize thread numbers
        err1_n=re.sub(r"\(\d+\)", "(X)", err1)
        err2_n=re.sub(r"\(\d+\)", "(X)", err2)
        match = (rc1<0 and rc2<0 and out1==out2 and err1_n==err2_n)
    print(f"{args} match={match} rc1={rc1} rc2={rc2}")

        print(f"  ORIG out={repr(out1[:1000])} err={repr(err1[:1000])}")

fn format_plain_node(node: &Node, show_icon: bool, show_suffix: bool, show_sym: bool, align: bool, _color: bool, is_child: bool) -> String {
    let mut s = String::new();
    if is_child {
        s.push_str("   \u{2514}\u{2500} ");
    }
    let is_dot = node.name.starts_with('.');
    if show_icon {
        let ic = icon_for(node);
        if ic.is_empty() {
            if align && !is_dot { s.push_str("   "); } else { s.push_str("  "); }
        } else {
            s.push_str(ic);
            if align && !is_dot { s.push_str("  "); } else { s.push_str(" "); }
        }
    } else {
        if align && !is_dot { s.push(' '); }
    }
    s.push_str(&node.name);
    if show_suffix { s.push_str(suffix_for(node)); }
    if show_sym && node.file_type=="symlink" {
        if let Some(chain)=symlink_chain_display(node) { s.push_str(&chain); }
    }
    s
}
